verdict: Positioning, pricing, objections and the honest preview sheet are best-in-class: every number matches the price list, nothing is invented, and the path from hero to Try box to Start free is short and clear at 1440 and 390 (9.99 screens at 390, 9.70 at 360, no horizontal scroll, no console errors). What holds it under 9.5 is the one moment that sells the product: on a visitor's own line the on-device demo misses the most common weak opener and sometimes explains a thin edit with a claim that is not true.
to_95: Make the Try box and final input catch the 'Here are N lessons I learned from...' / 'Here is what I learned after...' frame, so the commonest newsletter and founder opener gets a visible cut instead of 'Nothing to cut'.
Stop the Why line from praising a cliche or an over-length line: no 'It now opens on "It's more important than ever"' and no 'lands in one read' when the same result says it is over 280.
On the 'Not live yet' end state, give the visitor one honest next step besides the sample demo (a mailto to hello@hookworthy.com to hear when it opens).

issues.where: Try box (#try-ta) and final input (#fin-in), visitor's own line
issues.problem: Pasting 'Here are 7 lessons I learned from growing my newsletter to 10,000 subscribers in 6 months' returns 'Nothing to cut ... it stays as you wrote it'. 'Here is what I learned after losing $12k on one trade' does the same. This is the archetypal weak first line for newsletter writers and founders (audiences two and three), and the page's own promise is that it marks the fluff. The recovery copy ('Quick on-device check. In the app, Claude edits it and goes further' and 'Get three takes, free') is honest and good, but the visitor's first personal result still reads as the product failing on the exact case it exists for. 3 of my 10 pasted lines got nothing; 2 of those were correctly clean, this one was not.
issues.fix: Add the lead-in frames 'Here are N <things> I learned from/about', 'Here is/Here's what I learned (from/after)', 'N lessons I learned from' to the on-device frame rules so the line opens on the number and the fact (for example '7 lessons from growing my newsletter to 10,000 subscribers in 6 months'), with the cut words struck and tappable like every other cut. Add the same strings to the engine's test list so the homepage List starter and a real paste agree.

issues.problem: Two Why lines oversell a thin edit. 'In today's fast-paced world, it's more important than ever to really focus on your customers' becomes 'It's more important than ever to really focus on your customers' with the reason 'It now opens on "It's more important than ever", not the run-up to it', which presents a stock phrase as the payoff and leaves 'really'. A 290-character line gets 'With 4 bits of fluff gone, "Maybe you should consider reading" lands in one read' directly above 'Over 280 for one X post'.
issues.fix: When the new opening is itself a stock phrase or hedge ('more important than ever', 'maybe you should'), use the neutral reason ('The run-up went. The rest is yours to tighten.') rather than quoting it as the hook, and never say 'lands in one read' when the long/over-280 note is shown. Flag 'really' as a your-call word, as 'Maybe' already is.

issues.where: Signup sheet, 'Not live yet' state after Continue with X, Google or email
issues.problem: The state is honest ('no account was made ... Your email wasn't saved'), but the only ways forward are the sample demo or back to the page. A visitor who just chose Pro has no way to hear when it opens, so the strongest intent on the page ends with nothing kept.
issues.fix: Add one text link under 'Open the working demo': 'Want to know when it opens? Write to hello@hookworthy.com' as a mailto. No backend, no stored data, and it stays true to the preview.

issues.where: Free plan, first bullet sub-line 'Past 300 a day, Sharpen runs on your device. Still free.'
issues.problem: The first detail under the headline promise 'Sharpening is free. Forever.' is a cap written in engine terms. It is honest, but almost nobody writes 300 lines a day, and 'runs on your device' means nothing to a buyer who has not read the FAQ, so it plants a doubt in the row meant to remove one.
issues.fix: Keep the fact, change the framing: 'No daily limit you will notice: past 300 a day it switches to the quick on-device check. Still free.' or move the sentence into 'See everything included'.

issues.where: FAQ, 'What can it do with my X account?'
issues.problem: The answer opens with 'This preview doesn't connect to X', which answers a question about the preview before the question the buyer asked about the product. The strong part (never DMs, deletes or retweets; revoke anytime) comes second.
issues.fix: Lead with the product answer: 'It posts what you schedule, and nothing else. It never DMs, deletes or retweets for you, and you can revoke access anytime in X's settings. This preview doesn't connect to X at all.'
